payload.claim: `until.isoformat()` writes `until_ts` in `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` form (ISO with a 'T'), while every other timestamp this schema stores (`started_at`, `ended_at`, and every `datetime('now')` call elsewhere in ledger.py) is SQLite's `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (space-separated). The schema's own comment on `batches` (ledger.py ~line 27-30) states timestamps are TEXT 'matching every other timestamp this module writes ... rather than inventing a second representation' — this line does exactly that. Nothing in this diff or the passing suite reads `until_ts` back for a string comparison against another timestamp column, so no gate or test can see it, but a future lexicographic comparison (e.g. `until_ts < datetime('now')` in a recovery or report query) will misorder because `'T' (0x54) > ' ' (0x20)` at the same character position for an otherwise-identical date-time.
